Solved with one demonstration request and one correct submission (no wrong submissions).

## Rule
The grid has a uniform background plus one or more solid, axis-aligned rectangular color regions. Scattered single-cell anomalies/noise may occur both inside and outside the rectangles. Restore each rectangle to its dominant color throughout its bounding box, and replace isolated exterior speckles with the background. Preserve the input dimensions and the locations, sizes, and colors of all true rectangles.

## Demonstration evidence
Demo input/output were both 23x18. The background was color 3. Three rectangular objects were retained and repaired:
- color 0: rows 0–5, columns 3–7 (6x5);
- color 1: rows 1–5, columns 12–17 (5x6);
- color 1: rows 14–17, columns 3–9 (4x7).
Within these boxes, anomalous cells were restored to the rectangle color. All isolated colored cells elsewhere were changed to background 3.

## Solved test evidence
Test input/output were 11x26, background color 6. The two true rectangles were:
- color 8: rows 3–4, columns 15–21 (2x7);
- color 5: rows 5–10, columns 6–11 (6x6).
The single-cell color-4 anomalies within the boxes were corrected to their object color. All exterior color-4 speckles were removed to background 6. Submission was confirmed correct.

## Practical method
1. Identify the background, then locate coherent rectangular regions by repeated rows/columns and their dominant fill colors.
2. Use the rectangle boundaries, not individual pixel color, to distinguish internal corruptions from external noise.
3. Fill each rectangle uniformly with its dominant color; reset every other non-background isolated speckle to background.
4. Preserve grid size and check for all separate rectangles, including same-color rectangles that are disconnected.

Careful not to confuse this with tasks where isolated marks encode positions or objects: here the demo confirms scattered exterior speckles are disposable noise."
